nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the hash map that sends each literal over the variables of $\varphi$ to the list of its implication-graph successors, that is, of the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from it to $m$.
nodes.title: Adjacency table of the implication graph

nodes.summary: 2-SAT characterization (Aspvall, Plass, Tarjan): a 2-CNF formula is satisfiable iff it has no empty clause and no variable `x` such that `x` and `¬x` reach each other in the implication graph.
nodes.title: 2-SAT characterization

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ in which every clause has at most two literals, the SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the SCC-based 2-SAT procedure

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns false if $\varphi$ contains the empty clause; otherwise it returns true if and only if no block of the strongly connected components computed for the implication graph of $\varphi$ contains a literal together with its complementary literal.
nodes.title: SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure

nodes.summary: In a clause with at most two literals, any two different members $a$ and $b$ are all of its members: every member $c$ of the clause equals $a$ or $b$.
nodes.title: Clauses with at most two literals

nodes.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ does not contain the empty clause and the empty clause is derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution, then there is a variable $x$ such that the literals $x$ and $\neg x$ reach each other in the implication graph of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Resolution refutations give contradictory cycles

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, there is an implication edge from $l$ to $m$ when some clause of $\varphi$ contains both $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or with $m$ as its only literal (so a unit clause $m$ gives the edge from $\neg m$ to $m$).
nodes.title: Implication edge

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal $l$ reaches a literal $m$ when there is a path of zero or more implication edges of $\varphi$ from $l$ to $m$; that is, reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the implication edge relation.
nodes.title: Reachability in the implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$, $m$ is reachable from $l$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, viewed as a finite directed graph on these literals, if and only if $l$ reaches $m$ by implication edges of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Reachability in the finite implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the finite directed graph whose vertices are the literals over the variables of $\varphi$, listed without repetition, and whose out-neighbours of a literal $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from $l$ to $m$, read from the adjacency table of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Implication graph as a finite directed graph

nodes.summary: A clause $C$ satisfies the invariant with respect to a CNF formula $\varphi$ when for every literal $a$ of $C$ there is a literal $b$ of $C$ such that the complementary literal $\lnot a$ reaches $b$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$ (by a path of zero or more edges).
nodes.title: Resolution invariant of the implication graph

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a 2-CNF formula when each of its clauses, viewed as a list of literals, has length at most $2$ (repeated literals are counted with multiplicity).
nodes.title: 2-CNF formulas

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of all literals over the variables of $\varphi$, each appearing exactly once, arranged variable by variable: for each variable $x$ of $\varphi$, the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is immediately followed by the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: List of the literals of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal over $\varphi$ is a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that the variable $x$ occurs in $\varphi$. These literals are the vertices of the implication graph of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Literals over the variables of a formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then the variable of $m$ occurs in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Implication edges end over variables of the formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a variable $x$, if the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ reaches the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, then $x$ occurs in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: A positive literal reaching its complement lies over a variable of the formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the complement of a literal $(x, b)$ over the variables of $\varphi$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$, which is again a literal over the variables of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Complement of a literal over a formula

nodes.summary: The complement of a literal $(x, b)$, with variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b$, is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: same variable, opposite polarity.
nodes.title: Complement of a literal

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a 2-CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment of truth values to the variables that satisfies $\varphi$. If the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from a literal $l$ to a literal $m$ and $\sigma$ satisfies $l$, then $\sigma$ satisfies $m$.
nodes.title: Satisfying assignments respect implication edges

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then it also has the contrapositive edge from $\lnot m$ to $\lnot l$, where $\lnot$ denotes the complementary literal.
nodes.title: Skew symmetry of the implication graph

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $l$ a literal over the variables of $\varphi$, and write $\neg l$ for the complementary literal. The successors of $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ such that the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$: some clause of $\varphi$ contains $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or as its only literal. They are listed without…
nodes.title: Successors in the implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each exactly once, in the order of their last occurrences when the clauses of $\varphi$ and their literals are read from first to last.
nodes.title: Duplicate-free list of the variables of a CNF formula

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
